findings.title: Tab animation frame-ticks are counted in refreshes, not ticks
findings.problem: The animation frame index is derived from `tick`, but `tick` is advanced by exactly one per refresh (line 343 `tick++;`) and never by the configured period `scheduledPeriod`. display.yml documents frame-ticks in Minecraft ticks ("20 tick = 1 秒"), so with the shipped tab.refresh-ticks of 20 a frame-ticks:20 animation advances one frame every 20 refreshes = 400 ticks = 20 s instead of every 20 ticks = 1 s. ArenaScoreboard does this correctly (`tickCounter += refreshPeriodTicks;` at line 383), which shows the tab path is an off-by-unit error rather than an intentional different semantics. Changing tab.refresh-ticks also silently changes animation speed.
findings.impact: Any admin-configured tab header/footer animation runs 1/refresh-ticks too slow — 20x too slow at the default 1 s refresh — so the tab list appears frozen in a way that cannot be corrected from display.yml; the same frame-ticks value animates correctly on the sidebar and wrongly in the tab list.
findings.trigger: display.yml tab.header or tab.footer contains an `anim:` line with 2-8 frames and tab.refresh-ticks > 1 (default 20); the refresh task renders the block every period and every viewer's frame is computed from the per-refresh counter.

findings.title: Disabling the scoreboard mid-game destroys boards with no re-show path on re-enable
findings.problem: When the effective switch turns false, this branch calls hide(player) for every online board owner (line 367), removes offline entries (line 369) and then stopTask() (line 372). hide() deletes the BoardState from `boards` and restores the main scoreboard, so the arena permanently forgets those players. When the switch is turned back on, refreshAll() finds `boards.isEmpty()` (lines 375-378) and stops; show() is only called from ArenaInstance#addPlayer (line 343) and ArenaInstance#rejoin (line 575). /hilltop reloadconfig re-reads display.yml and restarts the tab task (HilltopCommandHandler lines 428-435) but has no scoreboard re-show step.
findings.impact: An admin who toggles scoreboard off and back on (display.yml scoreboard.enabled or game-settings.yml scoreboard.enabled, both re-read by /hilltop reloadconfig) leaves every player already in an arena with no sidebar for the rest of the match; only leaving and rejoining or a new match restores it.
findings.trigger: Set either scoreboard switch false and run /hilltop reloadconfig (or wait for the next refresh), then set it true again while players are inside a waiting or running arena.

findings.title: Unmanaged tab contexts still overwrite other plugins' header/footer with empty components
findings.problem: pushHeaderFooter() runs for every online player on every refresh (refreshAllUnchecked lines 348-351) regardless of isManaged(). For a context explicitly switched off (tab.contexts.lobby/arena/spectator = false) the else branch builds empty header/footer and line 427 still calls viewer.sendPlayerListHeaderAndFooter(header, footer). Bukkit's header/footer is a single per-player value, so this send erases whatever another plugin set for that player. The comment at lines 354-357 states the rule for this exact situation — a context switched off means the plugin must not overwrite the tab layout another plugin set there — but the code applies it only to name/order (resetNameAndOrder), while the header/footer path still sends empty components; the javadoc at lines 396-400 documents the empty send, so the two policies in the same class contradict each other.
findings.impact: On a server that delegates the lobby tab to another plugin (the documented reason to set tab.contexts.lobby: false), Hilltop Village clears that plugin's header and footer for every lobby player on the first refresh after startup or after the context is switched off, and keeps it blank.
findings.trigger: display.yml tab.contexts.<context>: false while that context has players (for example the lobby); the refresh task pushes empty header/footer once per player and caches it so it is not re-sent until clearCaches().

findings.title: restoreAll resets name/order for players whose name/order the plugin never set
findings.problem: The "touched" set is the union of all four caches (lines 215-219), and lastHeader/lastFooter are populated for every online viewer on every refresh (lines 427-429) even when the plugin does not manage that context and never called playerListName/setPlayerListOrder for that player. The restore loop then unconditionally executes playerListName(null) (line 225) and setPlayerListOrder(0) (line 226) for every UUID in that union. The T5.1 contract in the method javadoc ("only restore players this plugin really touched", so that tab.enabled=false or tab.lobby=false does not wipe another plugin's layout) therefore does not hold: merely receiving a header/footer makes a player count as fully managed.
findings.impact: On plugin disable/reload (onDisable calls stop() then restoreAll()), tab names and list order set by another tab plugin are wiped for all online players who only received a header/footer push — including lobby players in a context Hilltop was configured not to manage.
findings.trigger: Server shutdown or plugin reload while another plugin manages tab names/order; restoreAll() runs after at least one refresh frame has cached header/footer entries for those players.

unverified: TpsDiagnostic#printDiagnostic contains no TPS window math of its own: it reads Bukkit.getTPS()[0..2] (1m/5m/15m) and Bukkit.getAverageTickTime() directly, so no tick-window off-by-one or division-by-zero exists in that file. Absence of a finding is not proof of correctness, only that these specific defects are not present in the source.

The class comments in TabListManager (lines 292-307) asserting that Paper's CraftScheduler re-queues instead of cancelling periodic tasks that throw were not independently verified (read-only audit, no Paper jar or source inspection); none of the findings depends on that claim.

No build or test execution was performed. Reachability is static: ArenaScoreboard#show is called only from ArenaInstance#addPlayer (line 343) and ArenaInstance#rejoin (line 575), and the only scoreboard config reload is HilltopCommandHandler#reloadconfig (lines 422-436), which has no scoreboard re-show step.
notes: The three files were read in full (ArenaScoreboard 762 lines, TabListManager 725 lines, TpsDiagnostic 119 lines). The scoreboard task lifecycle is otherwise sound: ensureTaskRunning checks isCancelled, empty boards stop the task, quit cleanup removes per-player state, and the fatal-error catch cancels before clearing the handle. The main inconsistency found is that ArenaScoreboard advances its animation clock by refreshPeriodTicks (line 383) while TabListManager advances its clock by 1 per refresh (line 343), which is finding S08-F1. TpsDiagnostic's only weak spot is the empty catch around World#getTileEntityCount (lines 75-77), which would silently report 0 tile entities if the API were absent; it was not reported because the target Paper 1.21.4 API exposes that method, so the defect is not reachable in the audited environment.
